name: Silver Bird Brooch
description: A silver bird brooch pinned to a dark scarf. Appears in the museum theatre across two scenes.
narrative_significance: The brooch serves as a mysterious marker of presence and connection to Mara. In the afternoon scene, it is worn by an elderly visitor who knew Mara and responds cryptically to questions about her. In the evening scene, the scarf bearing the brooch is left across a front-row seat, suggesting a deliberate placement or visitation. The brooch's appearance frames the recurring line 'If the bird sings twice, wait for the door,' linking it to themes of memory, haunting, and unresolved connection to the deceased Mara.
